title: Aerobic Decoupling Analysis
subtitle: Comparing Aerobic Efficiency Factor (Pace/HR) between halves: Negative (-) indicates strong fatigue resistance; Positive (+) indicates cardiovascular drift. Decoupling ≤ 5% confirms a rock-solid aerobic base.
notEligible: Not eligible for decoupling analysis (requires steady aerobic endurance running with sufficient distance)
goodText: Heart rate and pace remained highly parallel between halves. Minor cardiac drift is well within normal limits, reflecting outstanding aerobic stamina and metabolic efficiency.
warnText: Slight aerobic decoupling observed with mild HR upward drift or minor pace drop. Represents normal thermal strain and cumulative muscular fatigue during long runs.
badText: Significant aerobic decoupling detected (cardiovascular drift > 8% or notable pace drop). Indicates running above true aerobic ceiling, dehydration, or glycogen depletion.
hrSteady: Heart rate & pace remained exceptionally steady across both halves
hrIncreased: Cardiac drift observed: HR drifted upward in 2nd half
paceSlowed: Minor fatigue detected: Pace slowed in 2nd half
paceFaster: Negative decoupling: Accelerated smoothly in 2nd half with energy to spare
